# Results — Study 482 (VWMA-Crossover)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The believers' claim — **a
volume-weighted MA crossover beats the plain SMA crossover because it leans toward the bars
where real money traded** — encoded as a mechanical rule. VWMA_N = Σ(price·vol)/Σ(vol) over a
trailing window; a long fires when the fast VWMA (10) crosses **above** the slow VWMA (30),
entered at the **next close** (one documented lag), and we measure the forward 5/10/20/60-day
return — head-to-head against the **same-length plain-SMA** golden cross. Offline & deterministic
once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted (**total-return**) closes **and volume** for **SPY, QQQ, IWM, DIA, GLD** (public, no key) |
| Window | 2005-01-03 → 2026-05-29 (**As-of 2026-05-31**, partial June dropped; **21.4** years) |
| SPY fingerprint | `0a125ce4099b` (sha1[:12] of the close column, As-of slice) |
| Entries | **500** mechanical VWMA golden crosses (vs **465** plain-SMA crosses) pooled across the 5 tapes (fast=10, slow=30) |
| Timing / costs | causal trailing MAs; cross read on close of *t*, enter the **next close** (one lag); hold 5/10/20/60 days; **1 bp** one-way × 2 legs per trade |

> **Price-only vs total-return.** The ETFs are auto-adjusted (dividends reinvested) — labelled
> total-return everywhere. The Signal axis uses a basket of **surviving** liquid ETFs; this is a
> single-instrument trend study, not a cross-sectional anomaly, so survivorship affects only the
> drift baseline (which the random-entry control neutralizes). Volume is the raw traded share
> count.

## The signal — VWMA cross vs plain-SMA cross vs a drift-matched random baseline

The thesis test is **VWMA − SMA** (does volume-weighting add edge?); the Signal test is **VWMA
− random** (is there any edge over drift at all?). The one-sample *t* is the **misleading**
number — it measures the index's upward drift.

| horizon | n | VWMA | win% | one-sample *t* | SMA | Δ vs SMA | Welch *t* (vs SMA) | random | Δ vs random | Welch *t* (vs rnd) | net of cost |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 500 | +9.9 bps | 57% | +1.08 | +19.7 bps | **−9.8 bps** | −0.67 (*p*=0.50) | +22.4 bps | −12.5 bps | −0.76 (*p*=0.45) | +7.9 bps |
| 10-day | 500 | +54.6 bps | 63% | +4.03 | +71.7 bps | **−17.0 bps** | −0.88 (*p*=0.38) | +47.5 bps | +7.1 bps | +0.31 (*p*=0.75) | +52.6 bps |
| 20-day | 500 | +103.9 bps | 65% | +4.81 | +116.3 bps | **−12.4 bps** | −0.41 (*p*=0.68) | +56.5 bps | +47.3 bps | +1.45 (*p*=0.15) | +101.9 bps |
| 60-day | 495 | +267.6 bps | 69% | +5.31 | +304.1 bps | **−36.6 bps** | −0.67 (*p*=0.50) | +299.2 bps | −31.6 bps | −0.58 (*p*=0.56) | +265.6 bps |

Read it carefully. The one-sample *t* against zero looks spectacular (**+4.81** at 20 days,
**+5.31** at 60) — but that is **pure beta**: long-only entries on an upward-drifting index
inherit the drift. The two tests that matter both fail:

- **Thesis (volume-weighting adds edge?).** VWMA − SMA is **negative at every horizon**
  (−9.8 / −17.0 / −12.4 / −36.6 bps), and the Welch VWMA-vs-SMA *t* is **negative everywhere**
  (never anywhere near +2). Volume-weighting does not help — it very slightly *hurts*.
- **Signal (edge over drift?).** VWMA − random **never clears the desk's *t* ≥ 2 bar** (max
  Welch *t* = +1.45 at 20 days, *p* = 0.15). No edge over buying on random days.

## Per-ticker (H = 20) — volume-weighting helps in only one of five names

| ticker | nV | VWMA | one-sample *t* | SMA | Δ (VWMA−SMA) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY | 91 | +129.6 bps | +3.79 | +129.2 bps | **+0.4 bps** |
| QQQ | 93 | +184.8 bps | +4.12 | +157.7 bps | **+27.1 bps** |
| IWM | 104 | +74.4 bps | +1.37 | +94.8 bps | **−20.4 bps** |
| DIA | 99 | +97.6 bps | +2.42 | +119.3 bps | **−21.7 bps** |
| GLD | 113 | +49.2 bps | +0.91 | +88.1 bps | **−38.9 bps** |

Only **QQQ** shows a meaningful positive VWMA-minus-SMA delta (+27.1 bps); SPY is a wash, and
in IWM/DIA/GLD the volume-weighted cross *underperforms* the plain one. No coherent
cross-sectional benefit to volume-weighting — the hallmark of relabelled drift.

## Volume placebo — scramble the volume, nothing changes

The decisive "does the volume term matter?" test: keep the price path and the volume
**marginal**, but permute which volume attaches to which bar, so the weighting is destroyed.
If the volume-weighted lines genuinely carried information, the scramble would collapse the
result.

| test | observed VWMA-cross 20d return | placebo *p* | draws |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY shuffled-volume VWMA | +129.6 bps | **0.238** | 500 |

**24% of scrambled-volume VWMAs match or beat the real one** (*p* = 0.238). The volume
weighting carries no usable information — a randomly-aligned volume series does about as well.
"Volume-weighting adds edge" is busted.

## Synthetic positive control — the harness CAN bank a real volume effect

On a deterministic tape with a *planted* volume-led drift pulse (knob `edge` — informative
up-moves land on heavy-volume bars, so a VWMA leans in earlier than the SMA), the VWMA-minus-SMA
delta behaves exactly as it must — so the flat real-tape result is a genuine "nothing there",
not a dead detector.

| planted edge | nV | VWMA | win% | one-sample *t* | SMA | VWMA − SMA |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (no volume effect) | 75 | +42.8 bps | 52% | +0.72 | +34.5 bps | **+8.3 bps** |
| **0.60** (real planted pulse) | 43 | +1163.8 bps | 81% | **+7.17** | +1110.3 bps | **+53.4 bps** |

With no planted volume effect the VWMA-minus-SMA delta is a near-zero +8.3 bps (no false
positive); a real volume-led pulse drives the VWMA cross to *t* = +7.17, an 81% win-rate, and a
clean positive VWMA-over-SMA delta. The detector is live — so the negative real-tape delta is an
honest "the volume term does nothing here."

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The VWMA golden cross does **not** beat a drift-matched random baseline
  (VWMA − random Welch *t* never clears 2, max +1.45 at 20 days, *p* = 0.15). The impressive
  one-sample *t*'s (20-day +4.81, 60-day +5.31) are pure beta — the upward drift of long equity
  indices that *any* trend-following entry inherits.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** No residual edge once the drift is removed; costs only deepen the
  hole. The same drift is captured more cheaply by holding the index. Nothing to scale.
- **"Does volume-weighting add edge?" — BUSTED.** VWMA − SMA is **negative at every horizon**
  (Welch *t* negative everywhere), volume-weighting helps in only 1 of 5 names, and the
  shuffled-volume placebo leaves the result intact (*p* = 0.238). Weighting the moving average
  by volume adds no forecasting information over the plain SMA cross — and slightly subtracts.
